model_family.evidence: The detection module itself employs a Graph Neural Network enhanced with domain adversarial training to learn robust, cross-protocol features and handle class imbalance.

split_protocols.evidence: In addition, to verify the performance of the model in handling imbalanced encrypted traffic samples (a common problem in actual network environments), we perform stratified sampling on the above datasets to construct sub-datasets.

main_split.evidence: CIC-DDoS2019 Dataset [19]: Developed by the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity, this dataset includes real-time network traffic captured over two days: January 12, 2018 (training) and March 11, 2018 (testing).

easy_vs_hard_reported.evidence: The experiments are designed around five research questions: the necessity of active drift detection, performance comparison with existing SOTA methods, detection efficiency, ablation analysis of core modules, and performance stability under imbalanced samples and different drift scenarios.

shortcut_check.evidence: Ablation experiments further verify the necessity and synergistic effects of the three core modules: dual drift detection, incremental learning, and small-model replacement.
